correctness.rationale: The Gaussian factor representation gives conditionally iid lognormal e-values. The e-BH rejection event is an empirical tail crossing. Conditional Glivenko--Cantelli convergence plus a small-tail binomial bound reduces the large-K event to a deterministic crossing except at one common-factor boundary. Reparameterizing by the Gaussian survival quantile turns the boundary into a one-dimensional minimization whose derivative is the Gaussian hazard minus a constant; strict hazard monotonicity gives the unique minimizer. Dominated convergence then gives the displayed FDR limit. The standalone verifier independently checks the hazard root, scalar minimum, tangency, side-of-boundary inequalities, and benchmark constants.

value.rationale: The result answers a concrete dependence question left open in the e-BH source for a canonical likelihood-ratio family and quantifies a burst mechanism that marginal FDR bounds do not show. The alpha-independent first-contact rejection fraction is a structural feature: a rare common-factor excursion can produce a macroscopic false-rejection block even when the overall limiting FDR is small. The closed one-dimensional hazard formula is directly computable and separates dependence strength from nominal-level shifting.
